title: Invisible, inaudible
hookLine: look and it can't be seen, listen and it can't be heard (Tao Te Ching 14)

cards: Three tries. You look for it, and there's nothing to see. You listen for it, and there's nothing to hear.

You reach out to grab it, and your hand closes on air. That's how chapter fourteen of the Tao Te Ching begins. It sounds like a riddle, or a ghost story, but it's the book trying, once again, to describe the Tao.
Back in chapter one, it said the Tao that can be told isn't the enduring Tao. Today it tries the eyes, the ears and the hands.

teach.h: YI, XI, WEI: THREE NAMES FOR MISSING.
teach.b: First, three names for a failure. What the eye can't find, the chapter calls yi: level and plain, nothing sticking out. What the ear can't catch, it calls xi: faint, rare, almost not there.
What the hand can't hold, it calls wei: tiny, subtle. Translators render these in different ways, but each name describes something missing.
Second, the three blend into one. They can't be pulled apart and examined; they merge. Not three hidden things, but one thing that escapes every way of grabbing.
Third, the shape with no shape. Its top isn't bright, the chapter says, and its bottom isn't dark.
Go to meet it and you won't see its front; follow it and you won't see its back. Like looking for the edges of the dark in a room with the lights off: there aren't any to find.
Fourth, why bother with something you can't see?

teach.h: HOLD THE OLD WAY, MEET THE NOW.
teach.b: Near its end the chapter turns practical: hold on to the ancient way, and you can handle what's in front of you now.

teach.h: LOOK, AND IT CAN'T BE SEEN.
teach.b: Some readers hear this as the point of the riddle: what can't be seen isn't a puzzle to solve but something to rest in. And for the ears there's a small doorway.
Silence itself can't be heard, and yet anyone can listen to it.

how: Some readers of the Tao Te Ching sit with chapter fourteen in silence, listening past the sounds around them to the quiet the sounds come and go in.

games.q: you look for the Tao and see nothing. you listen and hear nothing. you reach and grab air. what does chapter fourteen do next?
o: name each failure, and say the three blend into one.
describe what it really looks like.
games.why: the chapter names each failed sense, yi, xi and wei, then says they merge into one that can't be examined.

practice: Close your eyes and notice the sounds, a fan, traffic, a voice in another room, your own breath, without naming them for long.

Then turn toward the quiet underneath them, the space they appear in and fade back into; you won't hear it, and that's fine. Each time a sound pulls you, let it pass, and listen again for the quiet behind it.

wordCard.voice: Invisible. In chapter fourteen, what the eye looks for and can't find: the Tao, which escapes seeing, hearing and holding alike. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese: faint, rare. Chapter fourteen's name for what the ear listens for and can't hear.
